claims.text: An attacker who spent roughly 2 ETH drain $8.5M from Term Finance's Yearn-v3-based strategy vaults on August 23, 2026, while Term's core lending markets stayed untouched.

the attacker pulled approximately 2,843 ETH and 1.68M USDC — the latter swapped to DAI — into a consolidation wallet, a haul of roughly $8.5M representing about 68% of the vault product's pre-exploit TVL
route roughly 2 ETH through Tornado Cash, use it to acquire majority voting power over Term's thinly-held DAO governance token (TERM), then pass malicious proposals through that captured vote
The captured votes bought the attacker 100% voting control of 4 of Term's 5 USDC strategy vaults and roughly 91% control of the ETH Meta Vault
the attacker converting 44.37 WETH, apparently to fund gas or working capital — at block 25816049, roughly 06:25 UTC on August 23

I independently verified this on-chain: a live Etherscan fetch of wallet 0xD5183d8BfC65a50863C62aF2538198A8288FFc13 shows a balance of 2,843.2021 ETH (~$6.94M) and 1,679,642.45 DAI, and the address carries Etherscan's own "Funded By: Term Finance Exploiter 1" label
the trUSD contract itself was also locatable and identifiable: the ERC-20 ... is an upgradeable proxy with a max supply of 65,507,554.35 trUSD and 427 holders

Tori Finance's own documentation describes it as a synthetic dollar collateralized by delta-neutral trading positions that counterparty institutions run off-chain, plus an unspecified "additional buffer for adverse conditions"

KYC/AML-verified institutional participants can mint trUSD directly from the protocol at net asset value for a 10 basis point (0.1%) fee, while everyone else — retail users, unverified counterparties — can only acquire trUSD on the secondary market, swapping USDC or USDT for it on a DEX rather than minting it into existence

RockawayX's own "Tori Ecosystem Vault: Investment Thesis & Risk Disclosure" ... contains zero mentions of Term Finance, Term Labs, Term Vaults, or Yearn anywhere in its text. What it describes instead is infrastructure built on Upshift, an ERC-4626 vault framework ... plus a "Phase 2" allocation into Curve and Pendle
D2 Finance's own TVL sits at roughly $23.7M per DefiLlama — meaningfully smaller than Tori Finance, whose $50M Ecosystem Vault pre-deposit cap filled within seven days of launch

Its "Introducing Term Vaults" post describes Term Vaults as ERC-4626 tokenized vaults allocating capital between Term's own fixed-rate lending markets and variable-rate lending protocols elsewhere — Aave is the cited example integration
No search conducted for this research surfaced Tori Finance named as an integration partner or Risk Curator in that post
Maker's governance response was to mint and auction more than 20,000 new MKR ... The auction diluted MKR holders, DAI's peg held, and the protocol kept operating
Supply exploded toward 33 trillion tokens and the price collapsed to near zero within hours

the attacker who had manufactured roughly $116M in bad debt via price manipulation then used Mango's own on-chain governance to propose that the debt be paid out of the protocol's insurance and treasury funds — explicitly framing the theft as a "bug bounty." Roughly $70M of treasury was ultimately paid out in the settlement

Aave's January 2023 resolution of roughly 2.6-2.7M CRV in bad debt (left over from a failed exploit attempt against a CRV short) went further in the conservative direction: a governance-approved treasury buyback, no AAVE minted, no dilution, no exposure to GHO's peg

An attacker spent $4.4M buying BONK tokens purely for voting power, then passed a proposal authorizing a $20M payout to itself — a proposal that sailed through because the protocol had no timelock and no quorum minimum at all

Roughly $116M of that month's $247.4M is commonly attributed to a "Coldcard exploit" ... the underlying flaw was a firmware/RNG defect: a build flag had been zeroing a random-number-generator macro since March 2021, letting attackers brute-force weak seed phrases offline

By its own GitBook, D2 has operated live since December 2023, offering "institutional-grade Stablecoin, RWA, and BTC-backed structured strategies" through a DeFi-native protocol entity paired with an Approved Asset Manager entity registered in the BVI
The team is described only through background claims — "3 multi-billion dollar hedge funds," "ex-PAG quants" — that are not independently verifiable from public materials

It published on-chain forensic analysis of the April 2026 Kelp DAO/LayerZero exploit — roughly $292M — that was cited alongside independent researchers' findings in mainstream coverage of that incident
DefiLlama lists "Term Finance Vaults" as a protocol page distinct from the combined "Term Finance" listing, with the Vaults-only TVL layer sitting around $16.8M across four chains after the exploit
an April 2025 oracle decimal-mismatch bug caused unintended liquidations (~918 ETH, later a ~362 ETH net loss after recovery and reimbursement)

DefiLlama's classification puts 5 incidents in 2026 worth $25.1M combined before Term Finance, led by BonkDAO's $20M treasury drain in July. Term becomes the sixth incident in the category, bringing the year's governance-attack total to roughly $33.6M
Q2 2026 logged roughly 70-99 incidents totaling $746M — the most-hacked quarter in DeFi history by incident count
against a max supply of 65,507,554.35 trUSD across 427 holders, that mint is roughly 0.4% of supply
